p:cNvPr.descr: A simple diagram showing the general structures of blood glycosphingolipids as part of blood cell antigens. A the top is the O antigen (labeled right). It consists of a ceramide, which is labeled on the left and brackets the sphingosine, which is a labeled orange L-shape. The sphingosine bonds at the low right to a yellow rectangle labeled "fatty acid" and bonds down to a chain of sugars: a blue circle (Glc), which bonds right to a yellow circle (Gal), which bonds right to a blue square (GlcNAc), which bonds right to a yellow circle, which bonds down to a red triangle (Fuc). Below, the A antigen (labeled right) has a similar structure. It has the sphingosine and fatty acid, but the sphingosine bonds down to a chain containning Glc bonded right to Gal bonded right to GlcNAc, bonded right to Gal, which bonds down to Fuc and right to GalNAc (yellow square). Below this is the B antigen (labeled right). Here, the sphingosine is bonded right to the yellow fatty acid and down and right to a Glc, bonded right to a Gal, bonded right to a GlcNAc, bonded right to a Gal, which bonds down to Fuc and right to Gal.

p:cNvPr.descr: A table lists the symbols and abbreviations for common monosaccharides and some of their derivatives. • Abequose abbreviated as Abe. • Arabinose abbreviated as Ara. • Fructose abbreviated as Fru. • Fucose abbreviated as (red triangle) Fuc. • Galactose abbreviated as (yellow circle) Gal. • Glucose abbreviated as (blue circle) Glc. • Mannose abbreviated as (green circle) Man. • Rhamnose abbreviated as Rha. • Ribose abbreviated as Rib. • Xylose abbreviated as (orange star) Xyl. • Glucuronic acid abbreviated as (blue diamond divided diagonally) GlcA. • Galactosamine abbreviated as (yellow square divided diagonally)GalN. • Glucosamine abbreviated as (blue square divided diagonally) GlcN. • N-Acetylgalactosamine abbreviated as (yellow square) GalNAc. • N-Acetylglucosamine abbreviated as (blue square) GlcNAc. • Iduronic acid abbreviated as (brown diamond divided diagonally) IdoA. • Muramic acid abbreviated as Mur. • N-Acetylmuramic acid abbreviated as Mur2Ac. • N-Acetylneuraminic acid (a sialic acid) abbreviated as (purple diamond) Neu5Ac. Note: In a commonly used convention, hexoses are represented as circles, N-acetylhexosamines as squares, and hexosamines as squares divided diagonally. All sugars with the “gluco” configuration are blue, those with the “galacto” configuration are yellow, and “manno” sugars are green. Other substituents can be added as needed: sulfate (S), phosphate (P), O-acetyl (OAc), or O-methyl (OMe).
